title: The Sons of the Prophets
lead: "Sons of the prophets" (bene hannevi'im) is the Hebrew name for communities of prophets and their disciples in the northern kingdom in the days of Elijah and Elisha. They lived in groups at Bethel, Jericho and Gilgal, married and kept households, sat before a master to learn, and ran his errands. Earlier, Samuel led bands of prophets (1 Samuel 10:5; 19:20); later, Amos says he was not one of them (Amos 7:14).

sections.b: Bands of prophets appear first in Samuel's time, prophesying with music on the high place at Gibeah (1 Samuel 10:5–12) and at Ramah under Samuel's lead (1 Samuel 19:20). The phrase "sons of the prophets" begins in 1 Kings 20:35 and gathers around Elisha: fifty at Jericho stand some way off as Elijah and Elisha cross the Jordan (2 Kings 2:7), a guild member's widow is saved from debt (4:1–7), a hundred are fed from twenty loaves (4:42–44), they build a new meeting place by the Jordan (6:1–7), and one of them anoints Jehu (9:1–10). They call their leader "master" (2:3, 2:5; 6:5). Amos's reply to the priest of Bethel, "I am no prophet, and I am no prophet's son" (Amos 7:14), may set him apart from such groups.
